property_summary: For any caller address, the return value of approvedToLog must match the stored boolean value in the approvedLoggers mapping after the caller is set as an approved logger.
For any caller address that is the contract owner, approvedToLog should return true after the owner has set themselves as an approved logger.
The return value of approvedToLog for any address must equal the value in the approvedLoggers mapping for that address.
approvedToLog returns true for the owner after they set themselves as approved logger.
After calling setApprovedLogger with any address and status, approvedToLog should return that status for that address.
ApprovedToLog returns false for any address that was never set as logger.
After calling setApprovedLogger on a deterministic address, approvedToLog returns the value that was set.
Calling setApprovedLogger then approvedToLog for the same address returns the value set, regardless of previous calls.
After calling setApprovedLogger with any address and status, approvedToLog returns that status for that address.
For any caller, address k, and boolean status, if setApprovedLogger(k, status) is called then approvedToLog(k) returns status, even if the onlyOwner modifier reverts.
After a successful call to setApprovedLogger(k, true), a subsequent call to approvedToLog(k) returns true, even if other calls to setApprovedLogger fail.
After any setApprovedLogger call, the mapping should be updated to reflect the new status.
Regardless of reverts, the onlyOwner modifier ensures that setApprovedLogger can only be called by the contract owner.

After setApprovedLogger(msg.sender, true) succeeds for the owner, the call to approvedToLog(msg.sender) must return true; in the buggy version, setApprovedLogger always reverts, so the mapping never changes and these calls cannot happen.
Once a logger is approved via setApprovedLogger, subsequent calls to approvedToLog with that address should reflect the new status, regardless of who calls it.
The owner can always approve themselves by calling setApprovedLogger(address, bool) without revert.
logCreated returns true if and only if the caller is approved logger
If logCreated is called by an address that is not an approved logger, it returns false; if called by an approved logger, it returns true.
logCreated returns the same value as approvedToLog(msg.sender).
The return value of logCreated is the boolean negation of (approvedToLog(msg.sender) == false)
For any caller, the return value of logCreated is true if and only if the caller is an approved logger.
The function logRegisteredPubkey returns true when called by an approved logger with valid arguments.
Calling logRegisteredPubkey by an approved logger returns true.
Calling logRegisteredPubkey by an approved logger returns true.
For any caller, if approvedToLog(caller) returns true, then logRegisteredPubkey returns true.
For any caller, if approvedToLog(caller) returns true, then logRegisteredPubkey returns true.
The return value of logSetupFailed() is always true regardless of whether the caller is approved.
For any caller, calling logSetupFailed should return false if the caller is not an approved logger.
For any caller, calling logFraudDuringSetup should return false if the caller is not an approved logger.
For any approved logger, logFunded should succeed and return true.
When logFunded is called by an approved logger, the function must return true.
When logFunded is called by an approved logger, the return value must be true.

When logFunded is called by an approved (or unapproved) caller, the return value equals the negation of the revert guard condition (i.e., !approvedToLog(msg.sender) returns false when the call succeeds).
When logFunded is called by an approved logger, the return value must be true, and when called by an unapproved logger, the return value must be false.
For any caller, the return value of logFunded equals true when the caller is approved and false when the caller is not approved.
When the caller is approved, logCourtesyCalled returns true; when not approved, it returns false.
After calling setApprovedLogger with msg.sender as caller and true, logCourtesyCalled returns true.
After calling setApprovedLogger(caller, true), logCourtesyCalled returns true when called by the same caller.
After the owner sets the caller as an approved logger, logCourtesyCalled returns true when called by that caller.
logCourtesyCalled returns false when msg.sender is not approved, and returns false when msg.sender is approved (the bug makes it always false).
When logRedeemed does not revert, it returns true if and only if the caller is an approved logger.
logRedeemed returns true if and only if the caller is an approved logger.
Calling logRedeemed twice with the same arguments from the same approved caller emits exactly two Redeemed events.
After calling logRedeemed with an approved logger, the function returns true.
logRedeemed always returns true when it does not revert and the emit happens.
For any approved caller, logLiquidated always returns true.
When caller is approved, logLiquidated returns true; when not approved, returns false.
The return value of logLiquidated() must equal the approval status of the caller.
logLiquidated() returns true for approved callers and false for unapproved callers.
The return value of logLiquidated() must equal the approval status of the caller.
The return value of `logExitedCourtesyCall` must equal the negation of `approvedToLog(msg.sender)` (i.e., it returns true when the caller is NOT approved, false when approved).
The return value of logExitedCourtesyCall() must be false when the caller is approved, and true otherwise.
The return value of any log* function must be true when the caller is approved, and false otherwise.
For any log function returning bool, the return value must be true when the caller is approved, and false otherwise.
